text: Take the Pico 2, the 18650 cell and the slide switch from the parts catalogue and set them up in a declared layout. The Pico goes over the cell with both running along the length, the Pico's USB port points at one end, the switch handle points at one side wall, and nothing collides.

Inside the closed enclosure the 18.6 x 65.2 mm cell sits in a cradle and does not cut into any printed surface. It needs 3.0 mm of free room at both ends for the contacts and between 0.3 and 1.0 mm of side clearance where it is widest.
With the door shut, the cell may shift no more than 1.0 mm to the side or upward, and no more than 4.0 mm along its axis. It sits on the door, within 0.3 mm of the door's upper face.

The door is its own body on the bottom of the enclosure, 2.0 to 3.0 mm thick, and it slides along the cell axis, 0.25 to 0.35 mm of clearance on each side, coming out at the end away from the USB. A detent (0.3 to 0.8 mm deep) and an end stop hold it shut, and a grip sticks out 1.0 to 5.0 mm beyond the end wall. Along at least 60 percent of its length the door must overlap each side wall by 1.0 mm or more, and its outer face lies 0.3 to 3.0 mm above the bottom plane of the base.

If the door is off and the lid is on, the cell has to fall straight down out of the cradle through the bottom opening, without hitting anything. The opening is wider than the cell by at least 0.3 mm on each side.

The Pico is fixed on four posts below its mounting holes, each post having a pilot hole for an M2 self-tapping screw. Above the Pico's top surface leave at least 4.0 mm of free space, below its underside 2.0 mm, and keep it at least 0.3 mm from every wall. At each end of the cell there must be a passage for the cell wires, a hole at least 4.0 mm across through the shelf which does not open to the outside.

With the lid shut, you must be able to push a micro-USB cable all the way into the Pico via a single opening in an end wall, with at least 0.3 mm between the cable and the plug's envelope. No side of that opening may exceed the plug by more than 1.5 mm.

Keep the slide switch captive, within 1.0 mm in every direction other than toward its wire side, and leave 5.0 mm of free room behind its terminals. The handle comes out through a slot in a side wall and moves through its whole 3.5 mm throw while staying at least 0.25 mm from the slot. The slot may be at most 1.0 mm larger than the area the handle sweeps, and the handle should stick out 1.0 to 3.0 mm past the wall.

The top is closed by the base and a separate lid that you can remove. The lid sits on the base with a lip and a sliding fit and is secured by two M3 screws into bosses: lip clearance 0.15 to 0.35 mm, engagement 2.0 to 3.0 mm, lid plate 2.0 to 3.0 mm, and a total lid height of at most 6.0 mm. With the lid removed, the Pico and the switch go in along their own axes, and a screwdriver can get to each Pico screw and each lid screw.

When closed, the enclosure may only have the USB opening, the switch slot, the door seam (a gap of no more than 0.4 mm) and the screw holes, and at least 1.0 mm of material must surround every opening. Walls, shelf and lid are 2.0 to 4.0 mm thick.

Each of the base, the lid and the door is a single manifold body that can be printed on an FDM printer with no supports. On the bed, that means at least 25 percent of the base's plan bounding box and 50 percent of the lid's and the door's.
The closed enclosure must fit in 85 x 40 x 40 mm, with the long direction along the cell axis, and it has to stand on its base without tipping over.
What I get back: base, lid and door STLs, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own clearance report, with the report agreeing with an independent measurement.
